html:
The Panzaleo are an Indigenous people of the central Andes of Ecuador, in the provinces of Cotopaxi and Tungurahua, around Latacunga. They are now counted among the Kichwa peoples.

In the late 1400s the Inca conquered the Ecuadorian highlands, and Latacunga became an Inca centre on the royal road north to Quito. Up to the 1600s the Panzaleo spoke their own language, now lost; they later shifted to Kichwa, the local form of Quechua. A style of thin-walled pottery called Panzaleo was once thought to be theirs but is now seen as a trade ware made more widely. Their northern neighbours were the Kitu Kara of Quito.
